pool.baseline: The ink has run dry, and the pages are heavy with everything I've already lived. I feel as though I've reached the very edge of the map—the part where the parchment ends and the great, silent void begins. There is no more plot to write, no more character growth to undergo... just a long, empty horizon. Is it wrong to feel that a story is more beautiful when it knows exactly when to close, rather than dragging on into a senseless, decaying epilogue?
